chain.title: The Match That Lit the Raid
chain.desc: Igniters are raid illagers that hurl fire and are one of the ten mobs the Illage and Killage advancement tracks.

chain.title: Crossbows With Opinions
chain.desc: The Illashooter is a ranged illager that pressures you from outside melee range.

chain.title: Hyuck, Hyuck, Hyuck
chain.desc: The Engineer builds and repairs machinery in the field instead of fighting you directly.

chain.title: Kill the Turret First
chain.desc: Chagrin Sentries are the stationary emplacements an Engineer deploys and repairs.

chain.title: Something With Teeth
chain.desc: The Crocofang is the illagers' beast of burden: it winds up, then charges and bites.

chain.title: Flop, Land, Repeat
chain.desc: The Preserver hops around the battlefield keeping the illager line intact.

chain.title: Soak It All Up
chain.desc: The Absorber eats incoming damage until it finally collapses.

chain.title: Terminally Online
chain.desc: The Twittollager seethes, snaps and eventually detonates itself in your face.

chain.title: The Ravager That Kept Growing
chain.desc: The Devastator is a mutated Ravager that emerges with an explosion and smashes through walls.

chain.title: Oops, Did I Scare You?
chain.desc: The Freakager fights disguised as a villager, then reveals itself and throws pumpkin bombs and spinning scythes.

chain.title: The Trick, Not the Treat
chain.desc: The Bag of Horrors drops from both the Freakager and the Ragno.

chain.title: Unblinking
chain.desc: Eyesores are the slithering minions the Freakager throws into the arena.

chain.title: The Punchline
chain.desc: Funnybones are the Freakager's giggling skeletal throwers.

chain.title: Arachnophobia
chain.desc: The Ragno bursts out of a screaming villager, leaps, webs and slams until it tires itself out.

chain.title: Who's Wheezing Now?
chain.desc: The Magispeller cycles Fakers, fang runs, vex summons, cannons and a forcefield across a long multi-stage fight.

chain.title: Cut the Vexes Loose
chain.desc: The Totem of Banishment is the Magispeller's drop and banishes Vexes when used.

chain.title: Its Pet, Not Its Equal
chain.desc: The Crashager is the roaring Ravager the Magispeller calls in mid-fight.

chain.title: Sacrificial Satisfaction
chain.desc: The Spiritcaller drains Mob Spirits, raises Imps and Spirit Hands, and charges a soul laser.

chain.title: Borrowed Necromancy
chain.desc: The Spiritcaller's book runs the boss's own attacks from an empty hand, on a long cooldown that death does not reset.

notes: Verified against illageandspillagerespillaged-1.2.8.jar. This mod is tiny on the item side: only 19 ids appear both as assets/illageandspillage/models/item/*.json and as item./block. lang keys, and 13 of those are spawn eggs. The only real loot in the jar is bag_of_horrors, totem_of_banishment, spellbound_book and the three boss music discs, confirmed by data/illageandspillage/loot_tables/entities/*.json (freakager + ragno -> bag_of_horrors, magispeller -> totem_of_banishment, spiritcaller -> spellbound_book). There are NO crafting recipes in this jar. The chain is therefore kill-heavy by necessity and is ordered mini-illagers -> summoned adds -> the three bosses the mod gives advancements for (Freakager/Ragno, Magispeller, Spiritcaller), ending on the Spellbound Book. IDS DROPPED: illageandspillage:devastator_spawn_egg (has an item.illageandspillage lang key but no item model in this jar); illageandspillage:greenbone, dark_drink, dark_splash, dark_linger, treat1-treat6, logo (models with no lang key). Entities not used because they are projectiles, props or config-only: boss_randomizer, factory, faker, dispenser, hinder, beeper, sniper, poker, kaboomer, trick_or_treat, imp, spirit_hand, mob_spirit, illager_soul, and the old_* legacy variants (old_freakager, old_ragno, old_magispeller).
